instrument: Ordinance No. 2026-57 (emergency ordinance) - 12-month moratorium on planning, zoning, and building approvals for data centers, cryptocurrency-mining facilities, and substantially similar uses
term: 12 months from adoption (through approx. 2027-05-18); no extension found
notes: Council passed as an emergency measure on May 18, 2026 so it took effect immediately; blocks planning/zoning/building permits, approvals and certificates for data centers and crypto-mining facilities for up to 12 months while staff studies infrastructure needs.

instrument: Temporary moratorium on data centers (Henry Township Board of Trustees resolution; exact resolution number and vote date not located)
term: Unknown duration; source only confirms adoption occurred by March 13, 2026
notes: BG Independent Media (published March 13, 2026) lists Henry Township among 7 Wood County townships whose trustees had approved temporary data center moratoriums 'as of Friday (March 13)'. Could not find the township's own resolution text, exact adoption date, or stated term within the township's own web presence (woodcountytownships.com/henry has no ordinance detail); budget of ~4 searches exhausted without a primary document.

instrument: Ordinance amending City Code Chapter 157, adding Section 157.03 'Interim Use: Data Center Zoning Regulations Study' - one-year interim use moratorium
term: 1 year from adoption (through approx. 2027-07-09); City Council retains right to shorten or rescind
notes: City's own definition of 'data center' explicitly includes cryptocurrency mining and AI generation operations. Blocks building permits, rezoning, CUPs/variances, and re-platting for data center development citywide while a zoning study is conducted.

instrument: Ordinance (number not located) - one-year moratorium on accepting/processing applications for data center use
term: 12 months from adoption (through approx. 2027-05-27)
notes: Board of Trustees passed the ordinance at its May 27, 2026 meeting so staff can research and draft land use regulations. Ordinance number not found in accessible sources; several other secondary trackers (servercountry.org, lawweekcolorado.com) do not mention Milliken at all.

instrument: Resolution Enacting Moratorium (county document titled '2026-08-07 Resolution for Moratorium on Data Centers, BESS, Solar Farms') - 3-month moratorium
term: 3 months, from 2026-08-07 through 2026-11-06 (per county's own CivicAlert)
notes: Board of Commissioners approved a three-month proposal (amended from an original longer ask) covering new data centers, battery energy storage systems, and solar energy systems; applies only to new facilities, does not affect Putnam County's two existing large-scale solar fields. Vote was 3-1 (Hersey opposed, Wooten absent) per msgrnews.com; county's own CivicAlert states adoption date August 7, 2026 and end date November 6, 2026 (a news article gave a slightly different 'effective Aug 18' framing, but the county's own primary notice is treated as authoritative).

instrument: Ordinance No. 26-O-0011 - 180-day moratorium on new data center and battery energy storage system (BESS) approvals
term: 180 days from adoption (through approx. 2027-01-16)
notes: Applies in all zoning districts citywide; City Council unanimously approved it July 20, 2026 to allow time to study impacts and consider updated zoning rules.

instrument: Resolution R-26-06 - six-month moratorium on data center development in the Village
term: 6 months; exact start/end dates not confirmed
notes: Village of Clinton, Summit County, Ohio (near Canal Fulton) -- not to be confused with Clinton County or Clinton, Iowa/other same-named places. CivicIQ pages describing this resolution returned HTTP 403 / JS-rendered content that could not be read in full; information is limited to search-result snippets corroborated across two independent CivicIQ listings and one Facebook group post, which is weaker than the process's 'read pages, don't decide from snippets' standard. Could not independently confirm the vote date, exact term start, or full ordinance text within the search budget.

instrument: Application #26-25 - proposed text amendment to Town of Cromwell Zoning Regulations Section 4.2.E establishing a 12-month moratorium on data centers
term: Proposed 12 months; not yet adopted
notes: Primary-source Planning & Zoning Commission minutes (Aug 18, 2026 regular meeting) show the Commission voted 5-1 to accept the application and schedule it for a Public Hearing at a Special Meeting on September 24, 2026 -- i.e., only a hearing was scheduled, not final adoption. (A secondary aggregator, mytownview.com, incorrectly summarized this as the Commission having 'approved a text amendment... 4-1'; the primary minutes contradict that and are treated as authoritative.) As of the 2026-09-23 reference date, the hearing/vote had not yet occurred.

instrument: Resolution 26-R-07 - 90-day moratorium on applications for annexation, rezoning, variance, or conceptual site plans for data center development; superseded by Ordinance 26-O-12, which permanently prohibits new data centers in every City zoning district
term: Original: 90 days from 2026-01-29 (through approx. 2026-04-29); superseded on 2026-03-05, about 5 weeks in, by permanent Ordinance 26-O-12
notes: Primary-source city work-session action minutes confirm Resolution 26-R-07 was added to the agenda and passed unanimously on 2026-01-29. The city's own Data Center FAQ page states that as of March 5, 2026 new data centers are prohibited in every zoning district under Ordinance 26-O-12, which functionally replaced the temporary 90-day pause with a permanent ban before the 90 days had elapsed.

instrument: 12-month moratorium on new solar farm construction, adopted under N.C. Gen. Stat. Chapter 160D-107 (Moratoria)
term: 12 months from the July 20, 2026 vote (through approx. 2027-07-19); may be lifted early once the county's revised Unified Development Ordinance is complete
notes: Commissioners voted at their July 20, 2026 meeting; does not affect currently established solar farms. This is the county's second recent moratorium -- a separate 12-month data center moratorium was adopted in May 2026 (out of scope for this solar-specific entry).

instrument: Proposed temporary moratorium on commercial/large-scale solar facility development -- not yet adopted as of the latest information found
term: Not yet defined; county still studying legal grounds, scope, and cost of a possible narrow moratorium
notes: As of the June 30, 2026 article, County Planning Director John Eisler stated explicitly 'there is no moratorium in place at this time,' and that public hearings and written findings would be required before enactment. Commissioners had voted 2-1 to begin that process. No later news confirming actual adoption was found within the search budget, so this is reported as pending/proposed rather than active.

instrument: 180-day pause on new data center applications (Board of Commissioners), later replaced by a permanent zoning ordinance restricting data centers to conditional use in the I-2 heavy industrial district with size/setback/height/noise limits
term: Original temporary pause: 180 days from ~late February 2026; permanent zoning ordinance passed first and second readings in July 2026
notes: City Commission voted (reported Feb. 26, 2026) to stop accepting new data center applications for 6 months while studying impacts. After 'the last five-plus months' under that pause, the Commission approved a permanent zoning ordinance restricting data centers to I-2 conditional use, 1,500 ft. residential setback, 50,000 sq ft max floor area, 45 ft max height, 55 dB noise limit, plus a separate water-capacity ordinance capping aggregate demand at 2 million gallons/day. Exact day of the February vote and of final ordinance passage were not stated precisely in the sources read.

instrument: Six-month moratorium on data center development (Board of Supervisors resolution/motion; legality disputed since the township has no zoning ordinance and regulates land use only via its Subdivision and Land Development Ordinance, SALDO)
term: 6 months from the April 8, 2026 board meeting (through approx. 2026-10-08)
notes: The Board of Supervisors instituted the moratorium at its April 8, 2026 meeting in response to a 682-acre data center application (Linde Corporation) received April 30, 2026. Interim solicitor Ron Bugaj opined the moratorium is not legal under the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code because the township lacks zoning; prior solicitor also reportedly concluded a moratorium 'would not work' without zoning. The township is instead pursuing a SALDO amendment (and possibly future zoning) as the more durable regulatory tool. Status reported as 'active' reflects that the resolution has not been reported rescinded, though its legal validity is contested.

instrument: Ordinance 2026-02 - zoning text amendment adding Section 16.11 'Temporary Moratoriums,' authorizing (but not itself constituting) a Township Board moratorium of up to 12 months (extendable 6 months) on applications for existing, new, or emerging land uses including data centers
term: Enabling ordinance effective ~2026-05-12 (7 days after May 5, 2026 publication); any future moratorium resolution itself could run up to 12 months + 6-month extension
notes: Norvell Township pursued a deliberate two-step approach (per Feb. 17, 2026 board minutes, Resolution 2026-03 discussion): first amend the zoning ordinance to authorize temporary moratoria by resolution, then formally pause data center applications via a follow-on resolution once that authority exists. Step one (Ordinance 2026-02) is confirmed adopted May 5, 2026. No news coverage or township document was found confirming that the Board has since adopted an actual resolution imposing a data-center pause; township officials said in March 2026 there was no pending application and no urgency. Because what is confirmed is an enabling zoning provision rather than an actual pause, is_temporary_pause is marked false and status is reported as pending.

instrument: Resolution #2026-012 - Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers (unincorporated areas of Caroline County), one year
term: 1 year from adoption/effective date (2026-07-21 through 2027-07-21)
notes: Read the full signed resolution text. Suspends acceptance/processing of any application, petition, or hearing request for data centers in unincorporated Caroline County (does not apply to incorporated municipalities within the county). Directs the Department of Planning and Codes to submit a data-center report and recommendations to the County Commissioners no later than April 1, 2027.

instrument: Resolution imposing a Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers (18 months), adopted under Wis. Stat. Section 59.69(4)
term: 18 months from the date the resolution is published (through approx. late 2027)
notes: Read the county's own resolution draft (Executive Committee recommended it 8-1 on June 11, 2026; drafted by Corporation Counsel following an ad hoc committee authorized in May 2026). News source (WXOW) reports the full County Board approved it Thursday, June 18, 2026. Pauses receipt/granting of all permits/approvals for siting or construction of data centers (defined as facilities storing/processing >1 petabyte of data or consuming >2MW of electricity); does not itself prohibit data centers from locating within municipalities inside the county, which retain their own zoning authority.

instrument: Six-month moratorium on data storage facilities and data centers, extended by unanimous City Council vote
term: Original: approx. 6 months from ~January 2026; extended by unanimous vote on 2026-07-14 (new expiration not specified in sources found)
notes: Article (published after the July 14, 2026 vote) states the council 'previously placed a moratorium on the matter six months ago' and voted to extend it while City Attorney Linda McGrail drafts a permanent ordinance, explicitly waiting to see how courts treat similar ordinances elsewhere (citing a Hill County, TX moratorium that was struck down). Exact original adoption date, ordinance/resolution number, and the length of the extension were not stated in the source found.

instrument: Resolution imposing a temporary moratorium on acceptance/processing of applications for establishment or expansion of data centers (NAICS 518 data processing, hosting and related services)
term: 12 months from adoption; trustees may extend before expiration if deemed necessary
notes: Trustees approved the resolution to give the township zoning commission time to study impacts (land use, electrical demand, water resources, transportation, public safety) and recommend zoning amendments; article published April 20, 2026 but exact vote date not stated precisely.

instrument: Ordinance establishing a 12-month moratorium on battery energy storage systems (BESS)
term: 12 months from adoption (through approx. 2027-05-19)
notes: Read the city's own newsflash/press release. City Council voted unanimously on May 19, 2026 to prohibit acceptance, processing, and/or approval of applications for land development proposals relating to or incorporating BESS. Council also authorized the Mayor to send a formal objection letter to the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission (UTC) regarding a proposed Jupiter Energy BESS facility in neighboring unincorporated King County.

instrument: 12-month moratorium on data center applications
term: 12 months from adoption (through approx. 2027-02)
notes: This is the City of South Lyon, distinct from neighboring Lyon Township (which enacted its own separate data center moratorium around the same time over the 'Project Flex' hyperscale data center proposal). Article (published Feb. 11, 2026) reports City Council adopted the moratorium 'this week,' with a council discussion on a Tuesday -- consistent with a vote around Feb. 10, 2026, though the exact date and ordinance number were not confirmed in the source read.
